text: The first computer bug was an actual moth, found trapped in a Harvard Mark II relay in 1947.
Python was named after Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake.
The first version of the Linux kernel was about 10,000 lines of code. Today it's over 30 million.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed in the 1870s to reduce jamming on mechanical typewriters.
The term 'debugging' predates computers — engineers used it for mechanical systems long before software existed.
The first domain name ever registered was symbolics.com, back in 1985.
JavaScript was created in just 10 days by Brendan Eich in 1995.
The first computer mouse, invented by Douglas Engelbart, was made of wood.
Git was created by Linus Torvalds in 2005 after a licensing dispute over the tool the Linux kernel team was using.
The '@' symbol was chosen for email addresses in 1971 simply because it was unlikely to appear in anyone's name.
The first 1GB hard drive, released by IBM in 1980, weighed about 550 pounds and cost $40,000.
There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe, a fact often used to benchmark early AI search algorithms.
The floppy disk save icon still used in many apps today represents a format most young developers have never physically touched.
The first computer virus, Creeper, was written in 1971 and simply displayed 'I'm the creeper, catch me if you can!'
Ethernet was invented in 1973 at Xerox PARC by Robert Metcalfe.
The programming language C was developed by Dennis Ritchie between 1972 and 1973 at Bell Labs.
The first webcam was built at Cambridge University to monitor a coffee pot, so people didn't waste trips to an empty one.
Approximately 90% of the world's data was created in just the last few years, according to widely cited industry estimates.
The word 'spam' for junk email comes from a Monty Python sketch about canned meat, not the food company being at fault.
The first banner ad on the web, from 1994, had a 44% click-through rate — a number modern advertisers can only dream of.
GitHub's mascot, the Octocat, was designed to combine a cat and octopus because both are associated with dexterity and cleverness.
The first tweet, posted by Jack Dorsey in 2006, simply said 'just setting up my twttr.'
Ada Lovelace wrote what is considered the first algorithm intended for a machine, in the 1840s, decades before computers existed.
The USB connector was deliberately designed to be reversible after years of frustration — with USB-C, released in 2014.
The first email was sent in 1971 by Ray Tomlinson, to himself, as a test.
Stack Overflow was created in 2008 by Jeff Atwood and Joel Spolsky to fix what they saw as broken Q&A sites.
The term 'byte' was coined in 1956 by IBM engineer Werner Buchholz, deliberately misspelled to avoid confusion with 'bit'.
Wikipedia's servers run mostly on donated infrastructure and open-source software, not a large corporate budget.
The first iPhone in 2007 didn't support copy and paste — that feature arrived a year later.
Docker was originally an internal project at a PaaS company called dotCloud before being spun out in 2013.
The Y2K bug cost an estimated $300 billion globally to fix, largely due to two-digit year storage in old systems.
The first computer programmer, Ada Lovelace, never saw a working computer built in her lifetime.
Amazon Web Services began in 2006, originally to let Amazon rent out spare data center capacity.
The Rust programming language was named partly after a fungus known for being extremely robust and hard to kill.
The world's first website, built by Tim Berners-Lee, is still online today at its original address.
The 'Hello, World!' program tradition traces back to a 1978 C programming book by Brian Kernighan.
Bitcoin's creator, known only as Satoshi Nakamoto, has never been definitively identified.
The first 'like' button on the web appeared on FriendFeed in 2007, two years before Facebook adopted it.
MP3 compression was developed in the late 1980s by a team at the Fraunhofer Institute in Germany.
The word 'algorithm' comes from the name of the 9th-century Persian mathematician Al-Khwarizmi.
Windows 95's launch event reportedly cost Microsoft over $300 million in marketing.
The first practical touchscreen was developed in 1965 by E.A. Johnson for air traffic control systems.
Firefox's original name was 'Phoenix,' then 'Firebird,' before trademark issues led to the final name.
The average smartphone today has more computing power than the systems used to guide the Apollo moon missions.
The first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion was IBM's Deep Blue, defeating Garry Kasparov in 1997.
The '404 Not Found' error is rumored, though unconfirmed, to be named after a room number at CERN — it's actually just an HTTP status code.
The Great Firewall of China is not a single system but a distributed set of filtering technologies across ISPs.
Node.js was created in 2009 to bring JavaScript, previously browser-only, onto servers.
The first webcam-streamed event was a 1994 concert by the band Severe Tire Damage.
Kubernetes' name comes from the Greek word for 'helmsman' or 'pilot,' referencing container orchestration.
The first computer programming language, Plankalkül, was designed by Konrad Zuse in the 1940s but not implemented for decades.
Reddit's alien mascot, Snoo, was intentionally left genderless and faceless so users could imagine it as anyone.
The first gigabyte of storage that fit on a single consumer hard drive arrived in 1991.
TCP/IP, the protocol suite the modern internet runs on, was standardized in 1983 in what's called the ARPANET flag day.
The Enigma machine used by Germany in WWII had more possible settings than there are seconds since the universe began.
The Apache web server gets its name from being 'a patchy' server, built from a series of patches to existing code.
The first computer worm to spread across the early internet, the Morris Worm in 1988, was created as a research experiment.
The programming language Go was designed at Google partly to make large-scale software builds faster.
The first 3D printed object was created in 1983 using a method called stereolithography.
SQL was originally called SEQUEL, developed at IBM in the early 1970s.
The Wi-Fi symbol doesn't officially stand for anything — 'Wi-Fi' isn't actually short for 'Wireless Fidelity,' despite common belief.
The first item ever sold on eBay, in 1995, was a broken laser pointer.
React was originally built by Facebook for its News Feed before being open-sourced in 2013.
GPT-style transformer architectures, introduced in 2017, replaced older recurrent neural networks as the dominant approach in NLP.
The first computer game with graphics, Tennis for Two, was built in 1958 on an oscilloscope.
Instagram's first-ever posted photo, in 2010, was of a dog and a food truck in Mexico.
The concept of 'cloud computing' predates the term — timesharing systems in the 1960s offered similar shared-resource models.
The Raspberry Pi was originally designed to make programming more accessible to schoolchildren, not hobbyists.
The programming language Ruby was designed with a focus on developer happiness as an explicit design goal.
Google's original name during development was 'BackRub,' referencing its analysis of backlinks.
The first hyperlink-based hypertext system, ideated by Ted Nelson in 1965, was called Project Xanadu.
The C++ programming language began as 'C with Classes' before being renamed in 1983.
The first successful ransomware attack, the AIDS Trojan, was distributed via floppy disks in 1989.
npm, the default Node.js package manager, hosts well over 2 million packages.
The Great Internet Mersenne Prime Search has used distributed volunteer computing to find record-breaking prime numbers since 1996.
The Solidity programming language was created specifically for writing smart contracts on Ethereum.
TypeScript was developed by Microsoft to add optional static typing on top of JavaScript.
The first widely used version control system, CVS, was released in 1990, over a decade before Git.
The term 'cookie' in web browsers comes from 'magic cookie,' an older computing term for a token passed between programs.
The Commodore 64, released in 1982, remains the best-selling single computer model in history.
The original PlayStation used CDs instead of cartridges, a major shift that lowered game production costs.
The word 'hacker' originally referred to a skilled and creative programmer, not someone with malicious intent.
The Signal messaging app's encryption protocol is also used by WhatsApp and Google Messages for end-to-end encryption.
The concept of the 'null pointer' has been called its inventor's 'billion-dollar mistake' by Tony Hoare, who introduced it in 1965.
The Basic programming language was designed in 1964 specifically to make programming accessible to non-STEM college students.
WordPress powers a significant share of all websites on the internet, more than any other content management system.
The first successful spreadsheet software, VisiCalc, released in 1979, is often credited with making personal computers commercially viable.
GitHub Copilot, launched in 2021, was one of the first widely used AI pair-programming tools built on large language models.
The Tor network routes traffic through multiple volunteer-run relays, a technique originally developed by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory.
The first computer designed specifically for a single user, the Xerox Alto, introduced the graphical user interface concept in 1973.
The programming language Haskell is named after logician Haskell Curry.
YAML, widely used in config files today, stands for 'YAML Ain't Markup Language,' a recursive acronym joke.
The first robotic process to pass through a firewall to spread itself, the Morris Worm, unintentionally caused major early internet slowdowns.
Slack was originally built as an internal communication tool for a video game company before becoming its own product.
The average webpage today is significantly larger in file size than early versions of Doom, a common talking point about web bloat.
The first computer to fit on a single chip, the Intel 4004, was released in 1971 with about 2,300 transistors.
Modern CPUs can contain tens of billions of transistors on a single chip.
The Vim text editor traces its lineage back to the vi editor, first released in 1976.
The concept of 'object-oriented programming' was pioneered in the Simula language in the 1960s, predating C++ and Java by decades.
GitHub's contribution graph, the one developers try to keep green, was introduced in 2013.
The Perl programming language was originally created in 1987 for text processing and report generation on Unix systems.
The concept of 'Big O notation,' used to describe algorithm efficiency, was borrowed from a mathematical notation dating back to the 1890s.
